fire: A deterministic algorithm always produces the same output when given the same input.
Calling the hash function twice yields the same output for the same input string.

Pure functions return the same output for the same arguments and have no side effects.
Given the same input, the compiler must emit the same output on every machine.
quiet: A deterministic algorithm follows a fixed sequence of steps to solve a problem.
Calling the hash function twice is slower than caching its result.

Referential transparency makes programs easier to reason about and refactor.
